player.seasonOutlook: Kelce re-signed with the Chiefs and is returning for what might be his final NFL season. The veteran tight end's days as an elite producer are behind him, and he saw a notable dip in usage last season (19.6% target share was his lowest since 2014). Kelce did hold up for 17 games and still finished in the top 10 at the position in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards and fantasy PPG. Kelce has reeled off 10 consecutive top-five fantasy campaigns despite not offering much in the scoring department (he hasn't cleared five TDs in a season since 2022). The 36-year-old's role could dip even further this season, so he's best valued as a fringe TE1.

outlooksByWeek.7: Travis Kelce wasn't needed much in Kansas City's Week 6 win over the Chargers, catching four of five targets for 53 yards. The veteran tight end has slowed down after a fast start to the season, and through five games he's produced a 20-299-2 line on 27 targets while the offense has leaned heavily on Kenneth Walker. Kelce remains Patrick Mahomes' most trustworthy option, especially while Rashee Rice is sidelined. Kelce faces a tough matchup in Week 7 against a Seahawks defense that's allowed the fewest receiving yards in the league to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mahomes is a bit of a wild card as he embarks on his 10th season. The two-time NFL MVP followed up a pair of disappointing fantasy seasons (2023-24) with an elite start to 2025 (24.5 points per game during Weeks 1-8) and a disappointing finish that included 15.0 points per game during his final six games and a torn ACL in Week 15. Mahomes' efficiency has dipped the past three seasons, and while he made up ground as a rusher in 2025 (fifth among QBs in rushing yards and TDs despite three missed games), he might not be able to run as often this season as he recovers fully from the knee injury. Mahomes will be ready to play in Week 1, but he hasn't been a consistent fantasy QB1 since 2022. He's a risky mid-round flier in drafts.

outlooksByWeek.7: Patrick Mahomes didn't have much to do in Kansas City's Week 6 easy win over the Chargers. With Kenneth Walker and the defense doing most of the work in a 22-6 victory, Mahomes failed to throw a touchdown pass for the first time this season, although he did rack up 272 passing yards and 9.1 yards per attempt. His 8.3 mark on the year is his best since 2019, and through five games he's produced 10 TDs-nine passing and one rushing-against three turnovers. Mahomes faces a much tougher test in Week 7 against a Seahawks defense that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Rodgers re-signed with the Steelers and will return for his second season with the team. The 42-year-old is reuniting with his longtime head coach from Green Bay, Mike McCarthy. The duo will look to improve on a 2025 campaign in which Rodgers finished just outside the top 12 in passing yards and touchdowns while ranking 23rd among 28 qualified QBs in QBR. Even if Rodgers' efficiency improves, he remains a nonfactor as a rusher (he last cleared 107 yards in 2020) and hasn't been fantasy relevant since 2021 (25th, 18th and 25th in points per game in his past three full seasons). Even with a more pass-friendly playcaller and with Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard added to the wide receiver room, Rodgers is no more than a low-ceiling QB2.

outlooksByWeek.7: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers are in Paris for a Week 7 matchup against the Saints. He threw for 253 yards (33-for-49) with two TDs and one INT while rushing once for minus-one yard during Pittsburgh's 26-19 comeback win in overtime. Rodgers led four straight scoring drives to send the game to OT after the Steelers trailed 16-3 to start the fourth quarter. He now owns an 11:4 TD:INT over his last four outings, and he'll face a New Orleans defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points allowed per game (21.4) to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Chase is fresh off yet another elite fantasy season and he's now finished four of his five NFL campaigns no lower than fifth in fantasy PPG (the exception was 11th in 2023). Chase actually saw a big dip in yardage (1,740 to 1,426), TDs (17 to 8) and fantasy PPG (23.7 to 19.6) from 2024 to 2025 (which was no surprise with Joe Burrow missing nine games), but still put up big numbers thanks to pacing the league in pass routes and targets for the second season in a row. In fact, Chase's 125 receptions make him the third receiver in NFL history with 125-plus catches in multiple seasons. The 26-year-old remains the top target in a high-scoring Bengals offense, and is one of the top players in all of fantasy.

outlooksByWeek.7: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals are on the road for an AFC North showdown against the Ravens in Week 7. He corralled six of 10 targets for 77 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's 31-24 win in Week 5. Chase cleared concussion protocol in time to pace his team in all receiving categories, as no other Bengal had more than 25 yards or four targets. He'll once again be the primary offensive threat for Joe Burrow versus the Ravens' 22nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (34.1) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Adams' first season in Los Angeles was a success, as the veteran led the wide receiver position in touchdowns for the third time in the past six seasons. His 27 end zone targets were nine more than any other player and he now sits second in that category (148) and in TDs from scrimmage (117) since entering the league in 2014. Adams' ninth-place finish in fantasy PPG marked his ninth top-10 in his past 10 seasons. Now 33 years old, he isn't targeted as much as in years past (24% target share in 2025 was his lowest since 2016), but he's the clear No. 2 behind Puka Nacua in the Rams' elite, Matthew Stafford-led offense. Adams' heavy usage near the goal line helps cement him as a fine fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.7: Davante Adams was placed on Injured Reserve due to a ruptured left hamstring in the Week 6 loss to the Cardinals and is expected to be sidelined until after the Rams' Week 11 bye in a best-case scenario. With Adams out, names such as Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell should be in line for more targets, while established threats in the passing game like Puka Nacua, Tyler Higbee and Kyren Williams will also be in line for an uptick in numbers. Adams has 30 catches for 480 yards and four touchdonwns this season, and he will be sidelined for the time being, so he'll miss out on the chance of being productive in a favorable Week 7 matchup against a below-average Raiders defense.

player.seasonOutlook: The Chiefs have fielded a middling fantasy D/ST the past two seasons, scoring in double-digits only seven times  but finishing with zero or negative fantasy points only five times . Top draftee Mansoor Delane replaces CB Trent McDuffie, who was traded to the Rams, but the team otherwise returns largely the same starting lineup. An opening-week matchup against the Broncos should be avoided, but there are pockets of the schedule where the Chiefs would be great for streaming: Weeks 3-4 (@MIA, @LV) and Weeks 9-11 (NYJ, @ATL, ARI) especially.

Love was selected by the Cardinals with the No. 3 overall pick of April's draft. Love has good size and terrific speed (4.36 40-yard dash) to go along with a three-down skill set. He led this year's rookie class in both yards per carry (6.66) and yards after contact (4.16) while ranking second in forced missed tackle rate (3.5) during his collegiate career. He's a capable receiver at all levels, a competent pass blocker and protects the ball well (one fumble on 496 career touches). Love will immediately slot in as Arizona's feature back and, especially considering each of the past nine running backs drafted in the top 12 went on to finish top 12 in fantasy points as a rookie, he should be valued as a midrange RB1 with elite upside.

outlooksByWeek.7: Jeremiyah Love enters Week 7 with a questionable tag after missing Arizona's Week 6 game against the Rams with an ankle injury. The rookie has rushed 67 times for 245 yards and a touchdown while adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and another score through five appearances. His 3.7 yards per carry shows room for improvement, though his involvement in the passing game adds fantasy value. Denver has allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing RBs in 2026, creating an attractive matchup if Love returns. However, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight could complicate his workload even if he's cleared to play.

player.seasonOutlook: Robinson enters his fourth season having finished in the top five among running backs in carries, rushing yards, touches, yards and fantasy points in each of the past two seasons. Also a big factor as a receiver, he has ranked no lower than fifth at the position in routes, targets, receptions and receiving yards in his three pro seasons. In 2025, PFF tracked him with 86 forced missed tackles, which was easily the most among backs. The 24-year-old is in his prime and, though he has a new coach in Kevin Stefanski, his path to a massive offensive role remains clear. He's on the short list of players who should be considered with the first pick of your fantasy draft.

outlooksByWeek.7: Bijan Robinson is expected to remain the focal point of the Falcons' offense in the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Robinson logged a season-low nine carries in the Week 6 loss to the Bears, as Atlanta was trailing by 24 points in the second half. Despite this, he remained productive when given the opportunities, averaging 6.8 yards per carry. Expect Robinson to bounce back and remain one of fantasy's top running backs in Week 7, as San Francisco's defense has allowed 24.5 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs through five contests.

Brandon Aubrey managed one single, solitary extra point last game for Dallas. The Cowboys offense has sputtered of late, scoring a combined 29 points over the last two contests. Aubrey has registered just one field goal and two PATs over that span. In Week 7, Dallas will look to right the ship against another struggling NFC East squad, the Philadelphia Eagles. Philadelphia is allowing 22.8 points per tilt, which is 16th in the NFL.
